messages.subject: forecast count variable with forecasted variables - negative values- best approach?
parts:
Hi, 
I will try to be concise, and please note that despite working with R for a while, coding for forecasting with Rinla is a whole new thing to me. I am trying to visualize the predicted number of infected cases following different forecasts. I would really appreciate any help on the below: 
Using Rinla, I have selected the best model explaining the association between my outcome variable 'number of infected cases' and weather, socio-demographic variables....
The best model is: 
SA3.ar_rw6 <- inla(ninf ~ 1 + f(Year,model="ar1") + f(Month,model="rw1") + IRSADdecile + lag1.meanTmin + lag3.meanDailyVariationT + lag4.meanDailyVariationT +
                     soi + lag2.soi + lag2.Rainavg + lag3.Rainavg + lag3.nino34sst + lag4.nino34sst + lag2.nino34sstanomalie +
                     lag4.nino34sstanomalie +  lag1.avghostseekingfemales +WC,
                   verbose = F,
                   data = data,
                   family = "nbinomial",
                   control.compute = list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE),
                   control.predictor = list(link = 1))
summary(SA3.ar_rw6)

from this model, and after having collected and collated those forecasted variables under future climate change scenarios, I am having trouble with my results and am not sure I am using the right methods. 

I tried  several options: 
1. Run selected model with dataset combining actual data and forecasted data
run model selected > extract posterior summaries
example run SA3.ar_rw6Chistorical with dataset actualHistorical
##CODE: Extract posterior summaries
predictions1 <- inla.posterior.sample(1000, SA3.ar_rw6historical)
## Calculate the marginal posterior means and credible intervals
pred_means1 <- apply(sapply(predictions1, function(x) x$latent), 1, mean)
pred_lower1 <- apply(sapply(predictions1, function(x) x$latent), 1, function(x) quantile(x, 0.025))
pred_upper1 <- apply(sapply(predictions1, function(x) x$latent), 1, function(x) quantile(x, 0.975))
## Adjust lengths if there is a mismatch
min_length <- min(length(month_year1 ), length(pred_means1), length(pred_lower1), length(pred_upper1))
month_year1  <- month_year1 [1:min_length]
pred_means1 <- pred_means1[1:min_length]
pred_lower1 <- pred_lower1[1:min_length]
pred_upper1 <- pred_upper1[1:min_length]

## Create the data frame
marginal_df1 <- data.frame(
  MonthYear1 = month_year1,
  Mean1 = pred_means1,
  Lower1 = pred_lower1,
  Upper1 = pred_upper1
)

##visualize predicted outcomes
# Subset the data to include only every 6th month
every_six_months <- seq(1, nrow(marginal_df1), by = 6)
marginal_df1_6months <- marginal_df1[every_six_months, ]

# Print the first few rows to verify
head(marginal_df1_6months)

# Plot the marginal posterior means and credible intervals with MonthYear on the x-axis
ggplot(marginal_df1_6months, aes(x = MonthYear1, y = Mean1)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Lower1, ymax = Upper1), alpha = 0.2, fill = "blue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Marginal Posterior Means and 95% Credible Intervals",
       x = "Month/Year",
       y = "Predicted Outcome") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "4 years", date_labels = "%Y")

I obtain a plot with positive and negative values, which should not occur for a count variable. 

2. predict_inla 

# Ensure the model and prediction function can handle the extended timeframe
predicted_counts_historical <- predict_inla(
  model = SA3.ar_rw6,
  new_data = newdata,
  original_data = data
)
but this returns "  argument "df" is missing, with no default"
I tried to adapt the original function from github/gpw13/augury/R/predict_inla.R but in vain. 

Any advice would be so welcome. Thank you.

parts:
Here is a small example simulating new data. for new predictions, its easiest to
add those into your data with response 'ninf' = NA

then you can filter the output and only get predictions


n = 1000
x = rnorm(n, sd = 0.2)
eta = 2 + x
E = runif(n, min = 0, max=10)
mu = E * exp(eta)
size = 3
y = rnbinom(n, size=size, mu=mu)
r = inla(y ~ 1 + x, data = data.frame(y, x, E),
family = "nbinomial", E=E,
control.compute = list(config = TRUE),

xx <- inla.posterior.sample(10^3, r, intern = TRUE)
sim.new <- function(E) {
mu <- E * exp(Predictor)
size <- exp(theta[1]) ## variant=0
yy <- rnbinom(length(mu), size = size, mu = mu)
return (yy)
}

yy <- inla.posterior.sample.eval(sim.new, xx, E = E)
plot(E*exp(eta), rowMeans(yy))
